spans.s:
Puñji-ṣṭha is found in the yajurveda Saṃhitās and later, apparently meaning ‘fisherman,’ though Mahīdhara explains it as ‘bird-catcher.’ Cf. pauñjiṣṭha.
Foot notes Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 27; taittirīya Saṃhitā, iv. 5, 4, 2; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, ii. 9, 5; kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xvii. 13.
Āśvalāyana śrauta sūtra, x. 7; Pāṇini, viii. 3, 97.
On Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xvi. 27.

Puñjīla is found in the taittirīya Saṃhitā and the taittirīya brāhmaṇa in the sense of a ‘bundle’ of grass, being a variant of piñjūla.
Foot notes vi. 1, 1, 7; 2, 4, 3.
i. 7, 6, 4; ii. 7, 9, 5.
